caveats: Requires two caller threads invoking start()/stop() on the same SshServer/SshClient concurrently; duplicate start is contemplated usage per the start() javadoc ('Ignored if already started').

If the manager owns its executor (shutdownExecutor=true), a later full close shuts the executor down and terminates leaked tasks; the leak persists while the manager runs and whenever a user-supplied executor is used.
subclaims.reason: SshServer.start() (sshd-core/src/main/java/org/apache/sshd/server/SshServer.java:301) and SshClient.start() (sshd-core/src/main/java/org/apache/sshd/client/SshClient.java:447) are unsynchronized and guard only with check-then-act isStarted() (SshServer.java:305-307) with started.set(true) at the end (SshServer.java:348), so two threads calling start() concurrently both reach setupSessionTimeout (sshd-core/src/main/java/org/apache/sshd/common/helpers/AbstractFactoryManager.java:474), each scheduling a 1-second task (AbstractFactoryManager.java:479-480) into the plain field timeoutListenerFuture (AbstractFactoryManager.java:86); the second write loses the first handle, which stopSessionTimeoutListener (AbstractFactoryManager.java:491-510) can then never cancel, so the first task runs forever. Start-vs-stop also leaks: stop() sets started=false at entry (SshServer.java:361) while isClosed() stays false until close completes (sshd-common/src/main/java/org/apache/sshd/common/util/closeable/AbstractCloseable.java:138-140,169-172), so a concurrent start() passes both guards and can schedule a new task after stop's cancel-and-null, leaving it uncancelled. No common lock and no happens-before ordering exclude these interleavings; the started AtomicBoolean serializes stop-vs-stop only.
